This is the first paragraph. It has a specific claim about delegation. It spans two lines.
The second paragraph extends the idea concretely. Here is another paragraph in the second section.
Two semaphores, both env-tunable: global in-flight judge calls and a heavy-prompt cap.
Heavy judges hold both semaphores; light judges hold only the global one, so there is no deadlock risk.
Rate limits (HTTP 429) and transient overload (Anthropic's 529, plus 5xx) recover instead of gapping.
Backoff honors a Retry-After header when the API sends one, otherwise exponential backoff with jitter.
The manuscript under test is partly Claude-written, so a non-Claude judge is a more objective grader.
Version 0.1.0 of mash-core targets Python 3.13 and pydantic 2.9 with pydantic-ai 0.0.40.
The order id was 100200300400 and the run took 3.14159 seconds across 42 chapters.
A weighted mean rolls paragraph scores up to sections using char counts as weights.
Native scores are produced directly by a judge at its declared unit_type: paragraph, section, chapter.
Broadcast scores propagate a chapter-native score down to every paragraph with derived=True.
The ledger records total_cost_usd and a status of completed or halted_budget for each run.
Fixtures live in tests/fixtures and live tests are marked so they are excluded from the default run.
